terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation; transitive (what is broken off), or intransitive
evidence: Cato Agr. 38.2: ignem cavētō nē intermittās
Traupman 386: opus intermittere, to go on strike
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to leave off, intermit”: for a while, not for good (for that, see stop).

evidence: Cato Agr. 158.2: bibe, interquiēsce, deinde iterum eōdem modō
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “to rest between whiles, rest a while, pause”.

evidence: Cic. N. D. 1.114 (Lewis & Short): sine ūllā intermissiōne

terms.comment: Lewis & Short: ante- and post-classical. The word of the school break (see break).

phrases.latin: bibe, interquiēsce, deinde iterum eōdem modō, deinde tertium
phrases.english: Drink, pause, then do it again the same way, then a third time.

phrases.latin: paulisper alter alterīus cōnspectū, admīrātiōne mūtuā prope attonitī, conticuēre
phrases.english: For a little while they stood silent, each at the sight of the other, almost stunned with admiration for each other.

phrases.latin: Semper gaudēte. Sine intermissiōne ōrāte. In omnibus grātiās agite
phrases.english: Rejoice always. Pray without ceasing. In everything give thanks.

sources: Lewis & Short: intermitto · Lewis & Short: interquiesco · Lewis & Short: consisto · Lewis & Short: intermissio · Lewis & Short: mora · Lewis & Short: pausa
